prerequisites: It is recommended that the student has taken and passed the course 'Theory of Circuits and Electrical Machines', taught in the second year.

syllabus_topics: Block 2. Distribution networks and their integration into the electrical system.
5.1. Principles of lighting technology. Luminous magnitudes and units.

teaching_methods: Autonomous or group work (resolving proposed exercises, solving practical cases from lab, preparing lab reports)

assessment_methods.method: Problems proposed in class (submitted via virtual classroom)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, evaluation is continuous. The final grade is calculated as 0.2 * Practicals + 0.8 * Exam. A minimum of 5 points is required in each part (Practicals and Exam) to pass the course. Mandatory attendance to 80% of practical sessions is required to pass the laboratory practicals and final project. If a practical report is unsatisfactory, an exam may be required. For the extraordinary call, evaluation consists of laboratory practicals (20% of final grade) and a theoretical/practical exam (80% of final grade); students who did not attend 80% of practical sessions must complete a work/project. A minimum of 5 points in each activity (practicals and exam parts) is required. For unique evaluation, it consists of a theoretical/practical exam (80% of final grade) and a work/project (20% of final grade), with a minimum of 5 points required in each activity. The use of generative AI tools is allowed as auxiliary support, provided it is explicitly declared, but not to replace the student's own technical work or automatically solve problems.
